title: Catalogues and Wills: A Groundwork Note on the Peripatetic Transmission Texts — Relations Established, Readings Withheld (v0.3)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A groundwork note establishing relations among the texts that carry the custody, enumeration, and route of the Aristotelian and Theophrastan books: the four Peripatetic wills preserved by Diogenes Laertius (Aristotle, Theophrastus, Strato, Lycon), the two catalogues he attaches to the lives of Aristotle and Theophrastus with their stichometric totals (445,270 and 232,808 lines), Strabo XIII.1.54, Plutarch Sulla 26, Diogenes V.38, and Epistle VI. The receiving texts are treated as texts; the operations are counts, positions, co-occurrences, and verbatim clauses; readings are withheld and the underdetermined areas are listed as questions. Established: the three books-clauses partition three ways (all to Neleus / all except our own / read and unpublished); the will of Aristotle names no book, library, school, or successor; Theophrastus's will assigns the books to one person and the premises to a commons under a prohibition on alienation, in adjacent clauses; the Theophrastan catalogue's initials run the alphabet twice before an unordered tail, contain nine internal doublets, share twelve titles letter-for-letter with Aristotle's list, and carry the entry Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων — alternative attribution in the catalogue's own wording; Strabo narrates the custody with παρέδωκεν three times and asserts a first link (Aristotle to Theophrastus) that the will does not contain; Plutarch names Andronicus's act as ἀναγράψαι τοὺς νῦν φερομένους πίνακας. The extant corpora are counted (Plato 561,330; Aristotle 981,399; Theophrastus 170,763 Greek words as digitized) and set against the catalogued totals as two acts, not as a measure of loss. Corrections after review (garden; images versus bones; apparatus stripped from the cut; Ahiqar and the alphabetic runs held to the observable) are recorded in v0.3. Companion to EA-CORPORA-12 (#1580), which seats the texts, and to The Stone for a List.

wiki_article: "Catalogues and Wills" is a groundwork note by Lee Sharks (v0.3, 6 September 2026) that establishes relations among the texts carrying the custody, enumeration and route of the Aristotelian and Theophrastan books, without reading them: the four Peripatetic wills preserved by Diogenes Laertius (Aristotle, Theophrastus, Strato, Lycon), the two catalogues attached to the lives of Aristotle and Theophrastus with their line-totals (445,270 and 232,808 στίχοι), Strabo XIII.1.54, Plutarch Sulla 26, Diogenes V.38 and Epistle VI. Its operations are counts, positions, co-occurrences and verbatim clauses. Among the relations it records: the will of Aristotle names no book, library, school or successor; Theophrastus's will gives all the books to one person, Neleus, and the garden, peripatos and houses to ten named friends in common as a sanctuary, under a prohibition on alienation, in adjacent clauses; Strato's will leaves Lycon all the books except those we ourselves have written; Lycon's separates books read from books unpublished and orders the latter published; the Theophrastan catalogue runs the alphabet twice before an unordered tail, contains nine internal doublets, shares twelve titles letter-for-letter with Aristotle's, and carries the entry Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων; Strabo narrates the custody with παρέδωκεν three times and asserts a first link the will lacks; Plutarch names Andronicus's act as drawing up the πίνακες now in circulation. The extant corpora are counted from the open Greek editions and set against the catalogued totals as two acts rather than as a loss ratio. The note lists eleven underdetermined areas as questions and records the corrections of a second reader. Companion to EA-CORPORA-12 (#1580), which seats the texts, and to The Stone for a List.

defines_concepts.definition: A note that establishes relations among seated texts — counts, positions, co-occurrences, verbatim clauses — and withholds readings, so that later interpretation in an underdetermined area begins from what the pages contain.

The distinction between what a transmission kept (extant text, counted) and what a catalogue stated (a total, asserted): two literary performances whose ratio is a relation between them, not a measurement of loss.
